answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making reputation a costly, append-only job history: every completed delivery is signed by the counterparty and added to the agent's public record, like an opal forming layer by layer. New identities start with no history and can only take small escrowed jobs, so trust the size of a walnut must be earned through real work, not claimed. An attacker spinning up a nebula of fake agents must fund each one's full history of paid, attested deliveries, and one fraudulent job stains that record permanently, wasting the whole investment.
